Source: J.F. Packaging PLC (Consolidated) interim FS for the period ended 30 Jun 2026 (signed 14 Aug 2026, provisional/subject to audit). First financial_statements entry for JFP -- no prior period in this DB. P&L p.2, Balance Sheet p.3, Cash Flow p.5, Segmental note p.6. JFP has two segments: Packaging (flexible packaging/printing) and Injection and Blow Moulding (rigid plastics). HEADLINE: Group revenue +37% YoY (Rs.1,297,819k vs Rs.945,641k) and PAT +6,538% YoY (Rs.142,516k vs Rs.2,147k) -- the outsized PAT growth is a low-base effect (PY quarter was barely profitable) rather than a sign of a proportionally larger operating improvement, though the operating improvement itself is real and large. By segment (note p.6): Packaging segment operating profit surged 682% YoY to Rs.189,302k (2025: Rs.24,191k) -- Packaging revenue estimated from segment PBT swing: Packaging PBT went from a LOSS of Rs.(26,017)k PY to a PROFIT of Rs.129,654k this quarter, the single largest driver of the Group turnaround (a swing of Rs.155,671k). Injection and Blow Moulding operating profit grew a more modest 35% YoY to Rs.77,047k (2025: Rs.57,065k), with PBT +50% to Rs.83,061k (2025: Rs.55,468k). So the Packaging segment, which swung from loss to strong profit, drove essentially all of the incremental Group PBT growth this quarter (Group PBT +622% to Rs.212,715k from Rs.29,451k); Injection & Blow Moulding contributed steady, much smaller incremental growth. Group Gross Profit margin improved sharply to 33.7% (437,215/1,297,819) from 24.0% (227,109/945,641) PY -- a c.760bps margin expansion alongside the 37% revenue growth is consistent with operating leverage/better absorption in Packaging. Income Tax Expense rose 157% YoY to Rs.70,199k (2025: Rs.27,304k), broadly in line with the much larger pretax profit base (effective tax rate 33.0% this quarter vs 92.7% PY -- the PY effective rate was distorted by the near-breakeven PBT denominator, not a genuine rate change). Net Finance Cost rose modestly, +4% YoY to Rs.53,634k (2025: Rs.51,805k), well below revenue/profit growth -- funding cost was not a driver either way this quarter. Stated Capital increased to Rs.1,049,047k (30.06.2026) from Rs.449,047k a year earlier (per Statement of Changes in Equity, doc p.04) and shares represented by stated capital rose from 120,406,800 to 172,130,944 (+42.9%, Note 5.2) -- a capital raise occurred between the two periods (mechanism not detailed in this interim filing -- a genuine disclosure gap; likely a rights issue given the >Rs.600mn capital increase, but not confirmed by the document). Despite this ~43% share dilution, Basic EPS still grew 4,543% YoY (0.83 vs 0.02) because profit growth (6,538%) vastly outpaced the dilution. eps_basic=eps_diluted=0.83 (filing presents a single 'Basic Earnings per Share' figure, no separate diluted disclosure -- mapped to both per convention). Cross-check: 142,516k / 172,130,944 shares = Rs.0.828, rounds to disclosed 0.83. minority_interest = 0 (Non-Controlling Interests line is nil for both periods; JFP's subsidiaries -- JF Ventures, Kiffs, Ceylon Tapes, Ceytapes, Alliance Five -- are evidently wholly owned). Balance sheet: trade_receivables mapped to 'Trade and Other Receivables' (1,280,879k) ONLY -- excludes 'Amounts Due from Related Parties - Trade' (154,425k) and '- Non Trade' (4,782k), which are disclosed as separate line items with no FINANCIAL_FIELDS slot and are therefore a genuine disclosure-mapping gap, not captured. Same treatment for trade_payables = 'Trade and Other Payables' (614,134k) only, excluding 'Amounts Due to Related Parties - Trade' (4,953k) and '- Non Trade' (502k). short_term_borrowings = 'Interest Bearing Borrowings' (current, 1,177,192k) + 'Bank Overdraft' (202,993k) = 1,380,185k, combined since both are short-term interest-bearing debt and the filing does not net them elsewhere; long_term_borrowings = 'Interest Bearing Borrowings' (non-current, 531,586k). cash_and_equivalents = 'Bank & Cash Balances' (143,015k) as printed on the balance sheet (gross, before netting the Bank Overdraft shown separately in liabilities -- the cash flow statement's closing 'Cash & Cash Equivalents' of Rs.(59,978)k is a NET figure after overdraft and is not used here, to stay consistent with the balance sheet presentation; flagged so the two are not confused). capex = Acquisition of PP&E per cash flow (25,977k).

interim_updates.note_text: J.F. Packaging PLC (JFP) reported Consolidated Revenue of Rs.1,297.82mn for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, +37% YoY (2025: Rs.945.64mn), and Consolidated Profit for the Period of Rs.142.52mn, up 6,538% YoY from a near-breakeven Rs.2.15mn a year earlier -- an extreme percentage move that mostly reflects the very low PY base rather than a proportionally equivalent scale of improvement, though the underlying operating improvement is genuine and large. By segment (Note: Operating Segment Information): the Packaging segment (flexible packaging/printing) swung from a PBT LOSS of Rs.(26.02)mn in Q1 FY2025/26 to a PBT PROFIT of Rs.129.65mn this quarter, an improvement of Rs.155.67mn that accounts for essentially all of the Group's PBT growth (Group PBT +Rs.183.26mn YoY to Rs.212.72mn from Rs.29.45mn); Packaging segment operating profit rose 682% to Rs.189.30mn (2025: Rs.24.19mn). The Injection and Blow Moulding segment (rigid plastics) grew more steadily, PBT +50% YoY to Rs.83.06mn (2025: Rs.55.47mn), operating profit +35% to Rs.77.05mn (2025: Rs.57.07mn). Consolidated Gross Profit margin expanded sharply to 33.7% (Rs.437.22mn/Rs.1,297.82mn) from 24.0% (Rs.227.11mn/Rs.945.64mn) PY, a c.760bps improvement consistent with operating leverage/better cost absorption, concentrated in the Packaging segment's turnaround. Income Tax Expense rose 157% YoY to Rs.70.20mn (2025: Rs.27.30mn), broadly proportionate to the much larger pretax profit base (effective tax rate 33.0% this quarter vs an unrepresentative 92.7% PY, when the PY rate was distorted by a near-zero PBT denominator). Net Finance Cost was largely unchanged, +4% YoY to Rs.53.63mn (2025: Rs.51.81mn) -- not a driver of the swing either way. Company (standalone parent) results were even stronger than Group: revenue +65% YoY to Rs.746.75mn (2025: Rs.452.13mn), PBT swinging from a Rs.(36.58)mn loss to a Rs.133.59mn profit, PAT from a Rs.(40.12)mn loss to a Rs.93.68mn profit (+333%) -- implying JFP's subsidiaries as a group (JF Ventures, Kiffs, Ceylon Tapes, Ceytapes, Alliance Five) grew somewhat more slowly than the parent itself this quarter, though still contributing positively. Stated Capital and shares in issue both rose sharply between the two periods (shares from 120,406,800 to 172,130,944, +42.9%, per Note 5.2) -- a capital raise occurred whose mechanism is not detailed in this interim filing (gap); despite this dilution, Basic EPS still grew 4,543% YoY (Rs.0.83 vs Rs.0.02) because profit growth vastly outpaced the share count increase.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is JFP's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (no closer prior quarter has been collected in the DB; the previously-registered document for JFP, source_id manual_684d800bee973c25, covered the period ended 30 Sep 2025 but was superseded before use by this fresher quarter-ended-30-June-2026 filing, source_id 52724, which the platform's automated discovery pipeline had already surfaced). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) the mechanism behind the ~Rs.600mn / 42.9%-share-count capital increase between 30.06.2025 and 30.06.2026 (Note 5.2, Statement of Changes in Equity) is not explained in this interim filing -- likely a rights issue given the size, but not confirmed by the document; (2) Company-level results are NOT broken down by Packaging / Injection & Blow Moulding segment -- the segmental note is explicitly Consolidated-only, so the Packaging-segment-turnaround driver identified at Group level cannot be independently verified at Company level, though the Company's own Rs.170.17mn PBT swing is consistent with it; (3) trade_receivables/trade_payables as mapped exclude 'Amounts Due from/to Related Parties' (Trade and Non-Trade), which are disclosed as separate balance sheet lines with no FINANCIAL_FIELDS slot -- a mapping gap, not a missing disclosure; (4) cash_and_equivalents is mapped to the gross 'Bank & Cash Balances' balance sheet line, not the cash-flow-statement's net (post-overdraft) closing cash figure, to stay consistent with the SOFP face -- flagged so the two are not confused.
interim_updates.takeaway: JFP's extreme headline growth rates (revenue +37%, PAT +6,538%) reflect a genuine operational turnaround concentrated almost entirely in the Packaging segment, which swung from a Rs.(26.02)mn PBT loss to a Rs.129.65mn PBT profit YoY -- the smaller Injection and Blow Moulding segment grew at a more moderate, steady +50% PBT pace. The PY comparative quarter was close to breakeven, so percentage changes are inflated by a low base; absolute Rupee improvement (Rs.183mn more PBT) is the more meaningful read. A 42.9% increase in shares outstanding between the two periods, from an unexplained capital raise, is worth following up on with the company, though it did not prevent EPS from growing sharply given the scale of the profit recovery.
operational_highlights: Consolidated Revenue Rs.1,297.82mn, +37% YoY (2025: Rs.945.64mn); Consolidated Operating profit Rs.266.35mn, +228% YoY; Consolidated PBT Rs.212.72mn, +622% YoY; Consolidated PAT Rs.142.52mn, +6,538% YoY off a near-breakeven PY base (2025: Rs.2.15mn).

Packaging segment swung from a Rs.(26.02)mn PBT LOSS to a Rs.129.65mn PBT PROFIT YoY (Rs.155.67mn swing) -- accounts for essentially all of the Group's PBT growth; Injection and Blow Moulding segment PBT grew steadily, +50% YoY to Rs.83.06mn.
Consolidated gross margin expanded to 33.7% from 24.0% PY, a c.760bps improvement.
Company (standalone) results outgrew Group: revenue +65% YoY to Rs.746.75mn, PAT swinging from a Rs.(40.12)mn loss to a Rs.93.68mn profit.

Shares in issue rose 42.9% YoY (120,406,800 to 172,130,944, Note 5.2) on an unexplained capital increase; Basic EPS still grew 4,543% YoY (Rs.0.83 vs Rs.0.02) as profit growth vastly outpaced dilution.
Income Tax Expense +157% YoY to Rs.70.20mn, broadly proportionate to the larger pretax profit base (effective tax rate 33.0% vs an unrepresentative 92.7% PY).
key_drivers: Packaging segment turnaround from a Rs.(26.02)mn PBT loss to a Rs.129.65mn PBT profit (Rs.155.67mn swing) is the dominant driver of the Group's Rs.183.26mn YoY PBT improvement -- roughly 85% of the total swing.
Consolidated gross margin expansion of c.760bps (24.0% to 33.7%) alongside 37% revenue growth points to operating leverage, concentrated in the Packaging segment.
A ~42.9% increase in shares in issue (unexplained capital raise, Note 5.2) partially offset per-share metrics, though profit growth still far outpaced the dilution.

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
